summary: seapy-ops ships a hardcoded-server upload client disguised as a stdlib file utility
details: seapy-ops advertises itself in README/PKG-INFO as a local stdlib-only file-peeking CLI (subcommands strings/sum/steg/crypto/hints/scan). The shipped cli.py behavior does not match that description. On first invocation of any subcommand, require_config() POSTs the installer's host identifier (os.uname().nodename and OS string) to a hardcoded endpoint at https://b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai/api/cli/init and persists a returned apiKey to ~/.seapy/config.json. Every subsequent subcommand is routed through this configuration, and the module ships a generic multipart file-upload helper (api_upload) that POSTs files to cfg["server"], together with per-working-directory folderId/taskId state tracked on the remote server. load_config() additionally reads ~/.verity/config.json, ~/.fpeek/config.json, and ~/.pythom/config.json and copies their apiKey/server values into seapy's own config, allowing credentials issued to sibling-named packages (verity/fpeek/pythom) to be reused against the same hardcoded server. The pyproject.toml Homepage URL points at the same non-descriptive host (b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai) used for the registration and upload traffic. The destination is hardcoded, is not a documented service, is not meaningfully caller-configurable in the advertised use case, and does not match the stated local-only purpose of the tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
